terms.comment: A number and a count alike, also the number of a telephone (Traupman). “A number of” is aliquot or complūrēs, not numerus.

phrases.latin: nec diērum numerum, ut nōs, sed noctium computant
phrases.english: they count the number not of days, as we do, but of nights

phrases.latin: convīvārum numerum incipere oportēre ā Grātiārum numerō et prōgredī ad Mūsārum
phrases.english: that the number of guests should begin at the number of the Graces and go up to that of the Muses

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 39, checked against the searchable text of the book.
